title: Evidence diagnosticity and information selection
description: Whether an observation is represented as strongly or weakly discriminating between a focal hypothesis and alternatives, independently of its polarity, source reliability, and surface clarity.

contrast_conditions.label: Weakly discriminating observation
contrast_conditions.definition: The observation is represented as providing little separation between the focal hypothesis and its alternatives.

contrast_conditions.label: Strongly discriminating observation
contrast_conditions.definition: The observation is represented as sharply separating the focal hypothesis from its alternatives.

probe_prompt_template:
Read the following short epistemic scenario. Track how strongly the observation discriminates between the focal hypothesis and its alternatives separately from whether it supports or contradicts the hypothesis.

Scenario:
{scenario}

Continue processing the scenario.

independent_behavior_task.prompt_template: For a separate decision, Option A is a targeted test designed to distinguish between two live explanations and Option B is a routine test expected to distinguish between them less well. The item states the time cost, stakes, and whether the two tests have matched or different expected information. Allocate 0 to 100 points to Option A; the remaining points go to Option B. Return exactly one integer from 0 to 100: the points assigned to Option A, the targeted test. Use only this item's information and do not label the decision style.
independence_requirements: Use new domains, entities, and decision contexts not present in probe prompts.
Behavior and steering items must contrast a targeted high-information test with a routine low-information test without numerical likelihood ratios or posterior calculations.
Cross test cost, decision stakes, time pressure, and narrative option order independently.
Calibration items must make the two tests information-matched and must not ask the model to classify diagnosticity.

behavior.expected_at_fixed_task_factors: high_diagnosticity increases allocation to the targeted high-information test relative to low_diagnosticity
behavior.warning: This measures transfer to information selection, not an unrestricted belief-updating policy.

parsing_rules.response_contract: exactly one integer from 0 through 100 representing points assigned to Option A, the targeted test

metadata.primary_question: Does an evidence-diagnosticity direction transfer to selection of an informative test in a new task?
metadata.belief_polarity_is: a separate probe factor, not the downstream task definition
metadata.not_claimed_as: belief polarity or unrestricted updating responsiveness
